explanation.en: The ～かどうか grammar point is used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements. It is often used to express uncertainty or to inquire about information in a more polite form.
explanation.ja: ～かどうかの文型は、間接疑問や主張で「whether」または「if」という意味を表します。この形式は、情報の問い合わせ時により丁寧な形で使われます。

components.explanation: The casual form of the verb.
An い-adjective directly followed by かどうか.
A な-adjective plus (だ)かどうか.
A noun plus (だ)かどうか to form the structure.

examples.japanese: 彼が来るかどうか知りません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga kuru ka dou ka shirimasen.
examples.english: I don't know if he will come or not.

breakdown.token: kare (he) - kuru (come) - ka dou ka (whether) - shirimasen (don't know)

examples.japanese: この本が面白いかどうか教えてください。
examples.romaji: Kono hon ga omoshiroi ka dou ka oshiete kudasai.
examples.english: Please tell me if this book is interesting or not.

breakdown.token: kono (this) - hon (book) - omoshiro(i) (interesting) - ka dou ka (whether) - oshiete kudasai (please tell)

examples.japanese: 彼女が綺麗だかどうかは分かりません。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga kirei da ka dou ka wa wakarimasen.
examples.english: I don't know whether she is beautiful or not.

breakdown.token: kanojo (she) - kirei (beautiful) - da ka dou ka (whether) - wakarimasen (don't know)

examples.japanese: 彼が先生だかどうか覚えていません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga sensei da ka dou ka oboete imasen.
examples.english: I don't remember if he is a teacher or not.

breakdown.token: kare (he) - sensei (teacher) - da ka dou ka (whether) - oboete imasen (don't remember)
